definitions.gloss: dog and monkey; (figuratively) two parties who get along badly
definitions.explanation: Literally "dog and monkey," animals proverbially said to fight on sight. Used almost exclusively in the idiom {犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか} to describe two people on extremely bad terms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧だ。
examples.english: The two of them are bitter enemies.

examples.japanese: ⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧で、⟦ほとんど→ほとんど：00847_hotondo⟧⟦{話|はな}さない→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: Although they are brothers, they are on terrible terms and hardly speak.

examples.japanese: ⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧だった⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{協力|きょうりょく}→協力：00261_kyouryoku⟧し⟦{合|あ}っている→合う：10466_au⟧。
examples.english: The two countries, once bitter rivals, now cooperate with each other.

notes:
Almost always appears in the set phrase {犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧ ("on dog-and-monkey terms"), describing people who cannot get along. Rarely used alone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧: bitter enemies; on very bad terms
- {犬猿|けんえん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become bitter enemies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不仲|ふなか}→不仲：15745_funaka⟧: discord — plain description of a poor relationship, without the vivid imagery
